questions: Are we to output a single integer representing the XOR value of all simple paths from 1 to N (e.g., the XOR over the set of all such path XORs), or are we to find a path that yields a specific XOR value (e.g., the minimum or maximum XOR among all paths)?

If the output is a single integer representing the XOR over all simple paths, does the order of XORing the path XORs matter (though XOR is associative/commutative, the set of path XORs must be defined)?
Should we consider all simple paths from vertex 1 to vertex N, or only one specific path (e.g., the one with minimum XOR or some other criterion)?
Is the answer the XOR of the edge labels along each path, then XOR all those path XORs together, or something else?
If multiple simple paths exist, do we output the XOR of all distinct path XOR values, or the XOR of the multiset of path XORs (counting duplicates if same XOR appears from different paths)?

Does 'find the XOR' mean we should compute the XOR over the set of edge labels for each path, then output that value (i.e., one number per path), but the problem expects a single output, so likely not?
Are we allowed to assume that the XOR over all simple paths is well-defined (i.e., independent of order) and just compute that?
Should the output be the XOR of all possible simple path XORs, or the XOR of the edge labels in one chosen path (e.g., the path with lexicographically smallest edge sequence)?
